thread:
maya: Quick question for the design doc: should canary assignment be made at the edge LB or by a central controller? We need host-level affinity for cache warmups and a reliable automatic fallback if quality or latency regresses. Thoughts?

omar: Central controller is easier to reason about for rollbacks (single place to flip state) but introduces a control-plane dependency in the request path unless we push decisions out.

liz: Important distinction: host affinity (same worker host to keep KV/attention caches warm) != user-level sticky routing. Host affinity forces session stickiness even under rebalances. That has implications for autoscaling.

kevin: Edge decision reduces control-plane RTTs and avoids per-request RPCs, but you must distribute the full rollout logic and signals to every edge binary. Ops/testing surface increases.

maya: If we flip traffic to an unwarmed canary pool we see p99 spikes. Shadow warmup helps but only if the warmed host later receives the real user's traffic. So sticky mapping is critical.

dena: Hybrid pattern worked well in another org: control-plane publishes a short-lived signed rollout token to each region. Edges validate token sig + expiry and perform bucket assignment locally. Control-plane rotates tokens to change assignments.

omar: Token should include rollout_id, expiry_ts, bucket table, sticky_window_seconds, fallback_policy_id, signature. Edge only needs sig verification + hash to variant. If token expires, edge falls back to baseline.

kevin: Example token (pseudo):
```
rollout_id: r-2026-03-21-01
expiry_ts: 1765440600
buckets: [{canary:10},{stable:90}]
sticky_window: 3600
fallback_policy: "same-region->cross-region->lower-tier"
sig: "..."
```
Edge verifies sig and uses bucket table.

liz: Observability: token must carry rollout_id so traces can correlate. Edges should tag traces with rollout_id, assigned_variant, and warmed_cache boolean. Probes should emit warmed_cache=true/false and latency buckets.

emily: From SRE POV, fallback precedence needs to be explicit. Tenants may require region-first vs variant-first. Make fallback_policy configurable per-tenant and encoded as a small id in the token.

dena: For rotation: publish invalidation via region-local pub/sub for fast propagation; rely on token TTL as a safety net. Also include an absolute revision number so edges can reject out-of-order tokens.

omar: Agree absolute expiry + revision avoids ambiguity. Also include a compact fallback_policy id so edge can precompute fallback without extra lookups.

maya: Concern: if control-plane triggers an emergency rollback but pub/sub drops, expiry could be slow. Ops runbook should include a manual kill switch that rotates token to baseline and fires invalidation; escalation if propagation >30s.

emily: Yes. Add a manual rollback API that forces immediate rotation and publishes a short-circuit baseline token. Monitor subscriber ack counts.

kevin: Warmup cost note: reserving warm-only capacity for canaries is expensive. Alternative is shadowing: send sampled traffic to warm hosts (they process and mark as shadowed) so later real traffic hitting that user goes to warmed host. Need cost sim.

liz: Probe schema suggestion: minimal probe CLI -> control-plane event: "rollout_id, variant, probe_latency_ms, warmed_cache:true|false, error_count, sample_id". Keep it small and cardinality-safe.

omar: Control-plane computes a single canary_health score from aggregated probes: weighted error_rate, p99 latency, warmed_cache_ratio, any available quality signals. If health < threshold -> rotate token to baseline.

dena: Security: use short-lived signing keys stored in KMS; edge fetches public key bundle periodically. Sig verification must be fail-safe: unknown keys -> reject token.

maya: Action items: (1) prototype rollout-token format & edge verification (omar + dena), (2) draft probe schema + trace tagging (liz + emily), (3) cost sim for shadow warmup vs reserve (kevin + maya), (4) ops rollback runbook + invalidation SLA (emily).

deploy-bot: Queued: rollout-token-proto -> staging (#1302). ETA ~10m. :rocket:

omar: I'll open a compact token format PR today. Question: full fallback grammar in token vs short id resolved at edge? I vote shorthand id -> resolver at edge to keep token headers small.

liz: Shorthand id + resolver agreed. Also make rollout_id appear in biz metrics to tie alerts to active rollouts.

emily: I'll draft the runbook for emergency rollback and include an SLA for invalidation propagation.

maya: I'll write a short RFC summarizing the hybrid token approach, probe gating, and warmup simulation plan. Thanks all.
